page.title: Best Ultrasonic Cleaner for Carburetors (2026): Tank Size and Heater Tested by Owners
page.desc: The VEVOR 15L Upgraded fits small-engine and motorcycle carbs in a 13 × 11.8 × 5.9 in tank with a 600 W heater. See which size suits a bank of four carbs and when the Harbor Freight 6 Liter makes sense.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best ultrasonic cleaner for carburetors is the VEVOR 15L Upgraded ({buy:vevor-15l-ultrasonic-cleaner-600w-heater}): a 13 × 11.8 × 5.9 in tank with room for small-engine and motorcycle carbs, 360 W of ultrasonics, a 600 W heater and a drain valve. It costs less than Harbor Freight's 6-liter cleaner ($169.99 on 2026-11-14).

The most common owner complaint about cheap cleaners is a heater too weak to warm the tank. One owner of this model measured 59 °F to 131 °F in about 30 minutes, and filling it with hot tap water is faster still. For a bank of four motorcycle carbs or a stripped four-barrel, step up to the VEVOR 22L ({buy:vevor-22l-ultrasonic-cleaner-480w}): 19.7 in long, with 480 W across eight transducers. If you would rather buy in a store and carry it back if it fails, the Harbor Freight 6 Liter rates 4.7 of 5 from 530 reviews. It has a smaller tank and a 90-day warranty.

cells.power: 360 W / 600 W, degas and gentle modes

page.after:
What owners complain about

Slow heating came up most often (8 of about 25 owner reports we read). Heaters of 100-300 W take an hour or more to warm a tank, or never get it hot. The 15L's 600 W heater is the fix, and filling with hot tap water helps any unit. A tank too small for the carb came next (5 reports). In a 2.5-liter test, neither carb fit under the fluid, even taken apart. Noise (4 reports): owners add weatherstripping or a lid gasket. Units dying (4-5 reports): transducers coming loose, control boards failing, and heaters giving out after 18-36 months of daily shop use. Temperature overshoot (3 reports): the ultrasonics add their own heat, so check with a thermometer.

Which one by need

Small-engine, motorcycle or single car carbs at home: VEVOR 15L Upgraded, for its 13 in tank, 600 W heater and drain valve, and it costs less than the 6-liter Harbor Freight. A bank of four motorcycle carbs or several carbs at once: VEVOR 22L, which is 19.7 in long. Neither is deeper than 5.9 in, so take a four-barrel apart first. Store pickup and walk-in returns: Harbor Freight 6 Liter, at 4.7 of 5 from 530 reviews, but with a 6-liter tank and a 90-day warranty. The CREWORKS 15L has the same 360 W and 600 W specs as the VEVOR 15L, but it costs more on its maker store and was out of stock there.

Not recommended

Jewelry-size 1-3 liter cleaners for carbs: owners say carbs don't fit, and Harbor Freight's 2.5-liter unit runs five-minute cycles. Never run any cleaner dry, which can kill the transducers and power board. Never fill one with gasoline or spray carb cleaner, because the tank is open and heated. Use a water-based carb concentrate instead.

notes: Query choice: 'best ultrasonic cleaner for carburetors'. The current top results are mostly thin AI-style roundups (foliumbiosciences, sentinelmission, ovrclock, mobupps), plus maker blogs and forum threads, and they keep naming VEVOR 15L and CREWORKS 15L/22L. Pain points from about 25 owner reports (VEVOR store reviews, Canadian Hobby Metalworkers thread, RCN tests, plus search snippets from Grassroots Motorsports, Garage Journal and Yesterday's Tractors, whose pages returned 403): slow or weak heating 8; tank too small for a carb 5; noise 4; unit failure (loose transducer, board, heater after 18-36 months of daily shop use) 4-5; temperature overshoot or inaccurate dial 3; flimsy lid or handle 2. Segments: (1) home small-engine and motorcycle carbs: VEVOR 15L Upgraded wins ($135.90, 15 L, 600 W heater, drain; owner Doggggboy measured 15 to 55 °C in about 30 min) and costs less than HF 6L ($169.99) and CREWORKS 15L ($209.99, out of stock on maker store). (2) bank of four or multiple carbs: VEVOR 22L ($174.90, 500 × 300 × 150 mm, 480 W, 8 transducers). (3) in-store buying and returns: Harbor Freight 6 Liter (4.7 of 5 from 530 reviews, 90-day warranty, 370 W total). Amazon was not used (amzcheck walled); no amazon:us records. Prices read on vevor.com, harborfreight.com and the CREWORKS store (storecheck) on 2026-11-14. vevor.com is not Shopify, so prices came from WebFetch. The 15L buy box read '$ 135 90', which matches the category listing of $135.90; the variant tiles showed 'Out of Stock' while the buy box showed 'In Stock'. Unverified and kept off the page: the 15L's transducer count (listing says both 5 × 60 W and 2); 22L warranty length (page silent; VEVOR's 15L Q&A says all products carry 1 year; vevor.ca says 1-year warranty and 30-day returns); VEVOR US return-policy text (third-party guides only); Elmasonic Select 60 US price (snippets $1,948-$2,400, not read on a dealer page, so it's left out of the table); HF 2.5 L current price; CREWORKS 15L tank dimensions, drain and warranty. Codes: none of the four Awin codes appear on vevor.com or in search; terms unknown, cart test needed. The vevor.com Black Friday page shows $20 off $259, $30 off $359 and $45 off $559 coupons behind 'Get Code' buttons with no printed code, so they are not listed.
